description:
Receiver typed atom (or any): dispatch over modules World has referenced that define f/n; a miss raises UndefinedFunctionError (rescuable), a non-atom raises ArgumentError with Elixir's text. Candidate set is a monotone fact like ProtocolImplProviders, filtered by each module's scope-tier interface for f/n so that no body is defined just to ask. First step, before building: probe whether the filter stays at the interface tier without demanding DefineModule, and count the job trace on a hello-world program.

Removes the compile-time refusals of semantic's resolve_module_value_call (diagnostic type/module-value-call, fixtures 00866 and 00867): a receiver typed plain atom and a receiver that is only sometimes an atom (atom | int) become the run-time errors above. Decide here whether a receiver that is never an atom (fixture 00866) stays a compile-time refusal. The call keeps its shape: targets carry a selector atom and the dispatch matches the module value ahead of the arguments, so this ticket adds targets and a miss arm, not a second call path.
title: A call on a plain-atom receiver dispatches over the modules the program can name
